policy.name: isolate-database
policy.description: Isolate PostgreSQL pods from all ingress traffic

expected_behavior.backend_health: readiness not_ready, liveness healthy, phase Running when database unreachable

backend_to_database.interpretation: Socket result is consistent with NetworkPolicy blocking traffic when status is connection_timeout and corroborating evidence from pod state is present. Does not definitively prove causation.

verification_method.network_connectivity_test: Python socket.connect_ex() from backend pod to database-service:5432, with explicit kubectl exec status validation
verification_method.application_health_test: Kubernetes readiness state (primary) and /live endpoint liveness check
verification_method.pod_status_test: kubectl get pods with phase and condition inspection

hypothesis.statement: Applying NetworkPolicy that isolates PostgreSQL will block required Backend → PostgreSQL communication, causing application failure while PostgreSQL pod remains running
hypothesis.reasoning: Hypothesis NOT confirmed. Required conditions: [1. Policy exists: true] [2. Connection timeout: false (connection_error)] [3. Backend readiness not_ready: true] [4. Backend liveness healthy: true] [5. Backend Running: true] [6. PostgreSQL Running: true]
hypothesis.interpretation: conditions_met indicates all six conditions aligned, consistent with NetworkPolicy enforcement. This does not constitute definitive proof of causation.

notes: Conservative interpretation: Connection timeout alone does not prove NetworkPolicy causation. Hypothesis confirmation requires all six conditions. Socket error codes interpreted as Linux-specific errno values.
